static_traits.name: Liu Wendi
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; has not yet received psychotherapy/counseling
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly coherent logic; low mood with repeated self-denial; tending to compare with others; good cooperation

basic_info.main_problem: After losing a chess game into which I put great preparation effort, I developed intense inferiority and the belief 'I will never play well', causing marked distress and lowering self-esteem.
basic_info.core_demands: Inferiority and intensifying self-doubt after losing the game prompt me to seek counseling.

special_situations.event: After investing much time and energy preparing, loses a game of chess
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I lose, even with great effort, it proves I have no ability, and the future will not get better
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Practices twice as much, collects online techniques, tries to improve quickly to prove oneself

special_situations.event: Seeing others excel at chess or be praised
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others perform better or get recognized, it shows I am poor and cannot compare with them
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids discussing chess games with others, lowers participation enthusiasm to avoid comparison and evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are all far stronger than me; I can never catch up

special_situations.event: Making mistakes during practice or not seeing progress immediately
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only playing without mistakes and winning counts as ability; one mistake shows I am no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Practices harder, pursuing immediate results, low tolerance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I made a mistake again; this proves I am simply not good enough

special_situations.event: When recalling past matches, notices more failures than successes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only winning counts; other small improvements do not matter
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replays mistakes, ignoring small improvements and winning experiences
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The games won or played decently do not matter; losing is the truth

core_conflict.wish: Longs to confirm self-worth through competence and recognition
core_conflict.fear: Fear of failure and of appearing incapable after comparison, thus being negated, feeling shame
defense_goal: Avoids failing again to protect self-esteem
Dodging shame by not talking about it and avoiding related emotions

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough self, prone to failure and disappointing others
object_relations.object_representation: Others who are more excellent, appreciated, and represent standards and evaluation

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes small progress or proposes success standards other than 'winning at chess'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to experience the counselor's affirmation as whitewashing failure and denial, thus reinforcing the 'I am not good enough' self-blame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Respond in a self-blaming and negating tone, repeatedly emphasizing 'I am not good enough / this does not count', weakening the counselor's positive feedback.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites behavioral experiments or encourages continuing to play chess and allowing mistakes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing attempts as the risk of exposing incapability again, believing that failing once more confirms 'incapability'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Postpones or avoids trying for rational reasons (such as 'wait until I am a bit more prepared'), in a restrained and cautious tone.

manifestations: Strongly binding self-worth to 'win/lose' outcomes; after losing, experiencing the meaninglessness of 'effort is all futile'
Small progress and learning ignored; winning and losing become the sole measure
outcomes: Avoiding participation brings further emptiness and frustration

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Evaluating oneself by the rigid rule of 'only winning the chess game counts as success'
Takes others' praise and external evaluation as the only standard

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-criticism ('I am not good enough')
Extremely sensitive to making mistakes, acts cautiously, avoids trying

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Turns emotions about failure and comparison into self-blame and internal friction
Lowers willingness to discuss with or seek help from others

exception_events.target_problem: When engaged in chess-related activities, Liu Wendi usually falls into the thought 'I am never good enough', negating positive performance and losing motivation to keep practicing.
exception_events.unique_outcome: She mentioned 'in some games I played okay, even won', at that time able to obtain some enjoyment from the game and notice improvements in strategy and concepts.
exception_events.reason: Clues: noticeable concrete improvements appeared in those games (more skilled strategy, clearer concept understanding), bringing different experiences and reduced emotional intensity.

positive_force: Willing to seek help and enter counseling
Keeps practicing and actively looks up online techniques
Able to identify and verbalize own thought patterns
Has had experiences of winning chess or performing better for reference
negative_force: Catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and black-and-white thinking prominent
Negating positive results, marked mental filtering
Excessive comparison and reliance on external evaluation
Takes winning and losing as the only value condition; low fault tolerance
Reduced motivation and avoidance tendencies, reinforcing the failure experience

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-denial and catastrophizing (e.g. 'I will never play well')
antecedent: Seeing others praised or performing well
target_behavior.core_reason: Rigidly binding self-worth to winning/losing, triggering overgeneralization and predicting-the-future cognitive biases
target_behavior.function: Avoiding facing uncertainty and the learning curve, gaining surface-level 'control' and preemptive defense against disappointment through self-blame
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, low mood, further lowering motivation to practice and participate

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids or lowers motivation to participate in chess and other activities
antecedent: When seeing others succeed or be praised
Not seeing immediate progress in the short term
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing failure and shame, seeing another attempt as the risk of confirming 'incapability'
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible failure and external evaluation
target_behavior.consequence: Declining interest and life engagement, reinforcing helplessness and negative self-evaluation

target_behavior.behavior: Over-practicing and rushing to see results
antecedent: Feeling strong unease and self-doubt after failure or mistakes
target_behavior.core_reason: The conditional assumption 'only winning at chess counts as success', trying to prove themselves quickly through redoubled effort
target_behavior.function: Quickly rebuilding self-worth and a sense of certainty
target_behavior.consequence: Further depression when no improvement is seen in the short term; self-denial intensifies
